facts.boundary: Availability/preservation is local accounting, not a frozen whole peak budget. Effective transfer semantics, all donor accounts and failed transfer bookkeeping require complete source/config binding.
facts.fact: Quota limit is current Sandbox PD availability minus preservation (default 40*sizeof(long)*1024 RAM and 20 caps). Initial child quota deducts environment and metadata costs and is clamped to availability; transfers log allocation exceptions. Later upgrade takes min(configured increment, current limit); assigned bookkeeping increases before transfer_quota and transfer result is not inspected in that function. A future update can try remaining configured demand.

facts.fact: Downgrade makes at most four transfer attempts per quota kind and decrements assigned quota only for an OK return; remaining demand emits cooperative yield. Resource_request stores requested RAM/caps and triggers a report; replenishment occurs through configured assignment updates, not automatically in that handler. Yield response invokes another downgrade.

facts.fact: Quota_transfer considers invalid endpoint caps a no-op success and otherwise treats a result other than EXCEEDED as ok. Acknowledgement suppresses rollback; unacknowledged successful valid transfers attempt reverse transfer on destruction. Account.try_transfer calls transfer without checking its result. Routed_service returns INVALID when its PD accessor cannot supply a PD, and forwards actual transfer results otherwise.

facts.boundary: These per-process/per-descriptor counts do not bound all allocations, queued work, open-deleted backing or whole-domain memory.
facts.fact: The FD allocator has 1024 slots; each descriptor has 64 retained AIO handles and 64 AIO jobs. Closing AIO handles invokes Fs.destroy on retained Open_file pointers. Logical handle/job reset and descriptor metadata are distinct from provider storage and physical backing.

facts.boundary: No total registry-entry or backing-byte cap is established by this selected registry.
facts.fact: The private registry stores address, byte count and anonymous flag in metadata allocated from Libc::Allocator. Insert and remove are mutex protected; removal unlinks and destroys the metadata entry. The registry itself does not unmap memory or release the underlying RAM/provider backing.

facts.boundary: Upstream free, metadata destruction, pool retention and eventual kernel/provider physical release remain separate obligations; overhead() is not a whole-topology zero-overhead assertion.
facts.fact: Malloc_ram_allocator wraps upstream RAM allocations in separately allocated Registered<Dataspace> metadata and retains the successful upstream allocation by clearing deallocate. Release first invokes upstream RAM free, then destroys registry metadata; destructor visits each retained dataspace. The libc allocator delegates to malloc/free, with an interface overhead value of zero.

facts.boundary: Acknowledged quota transfer does not establish immutable total policy, complete call-site peak reservations or physical release. Quota_transfer/service implementations and selected policy remain outside these new texts.
facts.fact: Session creation reserves local session metadata costs and routes quota through child, reference account and service. Transfer failure returns resource errors; a session guard destroys metadata on early transfer failure. Upgrade accepts only the handed-out phase, attempts both quota kinds, reports transfer/initiation failures and acknowledges successful transactions. Policy supplies accounts, metadata backing, routes and initial quotas.

facts.boundary: A discarded client ID or destroyed metadata does not prove provider closure, successful quota recovery or complete physical reclamation.
facts.fact: Quota reversal attempts service-to-reference and reference-to-client transfers, acknowledges matching successful pairs, warns on failures and destroys session metadata. Close can return PENDING after initiating and waking the provider. CLOSED responses for vanished clients attempt quota withdrawal to the reference account and destroy metadata; transfer failures are explicitly reported. A capability delivered after client disappearance initiates close rather than merely dropping the state.

facts.fact: close_all_sessions first requests dynamic CPU-session closure, stops that loop on pending closure, destroys the initial thread, conditionally destroys CPU connection depending on kernel eager-destruction support, purges server session metadata, requests environment closes, discards client IDs for pending dynamic closes, closes PD and conditionally destroys CPU last. env_sessions_closed checks linker/log/binary and explicitly omits CPU state; its documented precondition protects environment state until servers close.

facts.fact: ELF loading attaches the image, allocates and locally fills writable segments, attaches them remotely and retains successful allocations; read-only segments attach the original ELF dataspace. Failures return load errors. The source explicitly relies on destruction of the distinct RAM session to regain earlier successful segment allocations after a later failure. Initial_thread destruction calls kill_thread; startup only occurs after successful loading.

Destructor delegates to env.close. Parent resource requests and availability signals are policy-mediated; yield is explicitly cooperative and the component is not obliged to comply. Child exit is a hint forwarded to policy, not immediate object destruction.
